ayahs.1: Alif-Lam-Ra. This is a Book We revealed to you so you may lead people out of darkness into light—by their Rabb's will—to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
ayahs.2: Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Woe to those who reject the truth for a severe torment.
ayahs.3: They prefer the life of this world over the Akhirah and block others from Allah's path, trying to make it appear crooked. They have gone far astray.
ayahs.4: We never sent a messenger except in the language of his people, to clarify for them. Then Allah leaves whomever He wills to stray and guides whomever He wills. He is the Almighty, All-Wise.
ayahs.5: We sent Moses with Our signs, commanding: "Lead your people out of darkness into light, and remind them of Allah's days of favour." In this are signs for whoever is steadfast and grateful.
ayahs.6: Recall when Moses said to his people: "Remember Allah's favour upon you when He rescued you from Pharaoh's people, who afflicted you with dreadful torment—slaughtering your sons and sparing your women. That was a severe trial from your Rabb."
ayahs.7: And when your Rabb proclaimed: "If you show shukr—gratitude in word and action—I will give you more. If you are ungrateful, My punishment is severe."
ayahs.8: Moses added: "If you and everyone on earth were ungrateful, know that Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy."
ayahs.9: Have you not heard of those before you—Noah's people, 'Ad, Thamud, and those after them? Only Allah knows their number. Their messengers came with clear proofs, but they covered their mouths and said: "We reject what you were sent with, and we are in alarming doubt about what you invite us to."
ayahs.10: Their messengers asked: "Is there doubt about Allah, Originator of the heavens and earth? He invites you to forgive your sins and grant you respite until your appointed term." They replied: "You are only humans like us. You want to turn us from what our forefathers worshipped. Bring us a compelling proof."
ayahs.11: Their messengers said: "We are only humans like you, but Allah favours whomever He chooses of His servants. We cannot bring you proof except by Allah's permission. In Allah let the believers put their trust."
ayahs.12: Why should we not trust Allah when He has guided us to the best ways? We will patiently endure whatever harm you cause us. In Allah let the faithful put their trust."
ayahs.13: Those who rejected the truth threatened their messengers: "We will expel you from our land unless you return to our faith." Their Rabb revealed to them: "We will destroy the wrongdoers,
ayahs.14: and make you dwell in the land after them. This is for whoever stands in awe before Me and fears My warning."
ayahs.15: Both sides called for judgment, and every stubborn tyrant was doomed.
ayahs.16: Hell awaits them. They will drink oozing pus,
ayahs.17: sipping with difficulty, barely swallowing. Death surrounds them from every side, yet they cannot die. Harsher torment still awaits.
ayahs.18: The deeds of those who reject their Rabb are like ashes blown fiercely by wind on a stormy day. They gain nothing from what they earned. That is the farthest straying.
ayahs.19: Do you not see that Allah created the heavens and earth for a purpose? If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation.
ayahs.20: That is not difficult for Allah at all.
ayahs.21: They will all appear before Allah. The lowly followers will appeal to the arrogant leaders: "We were your devoted followers—will you protect us from Allah's torment in any way?" They will reply: "Had Allah guided us, we would have guided you. Now it is the same whether we bear it patiently or not—there is no escape for us."
ayahs.22: Satan will say after judgment: "Allah gave you a true promise. I made you a promise too, but I failed you. I had no authority over you—I only called you, and you answered. Do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot save you, nor can you save me. I reject your past association of me with Allah. The wrongdoers will suffer painful punishment."
ayahs.23: Those who believe and do good will enter Gardens beneath which rivers flow, to remain forever by their Rabb's will, greeted with "Peace."
ayahs.24: Do you not see how Allah compares a good word to a good tree—root firm, branches reaching the sky,
ayahs.25: always yielding fruit in every season by its Rabb's will? This is how Allah sets parables for people, so they may take heed.
ayahs.26: The parable of an evil word is an evil tree, uprooted from the earth, with no stability.
ayahs.27: Allah keeps the believers firm with the firm word of faith in this dunya and the Akhirah. He leaves the wrongdoers to stray. Allah does what He wills.
ayahs.28: Have you not seen those who meet Allah's favours with ingratitude and lead their people to ruin?
ayahs.29: In Hell they will burn. What an evil place to settle.
ayahs.30: They set up rivals to Allah to mislead from His path. Say: "Enjoy yourselves briefly. Your destination is the Fire."
ayahs.31: Tell My believing servants to establish salah and give from what We provided—openly and secretly—before a Day arrives when there will be no ransom and no friendly ties.
ayahs.32: Allah created the heavens and earth and sends rain from the sky, producing fruits as provision for you. He subjected ships to sail the sea by His command, and subjected rivers for you.
ayahs.33: He subjected the sun and moon, each in constant orbit, and subjected day and night for you.
ayahs.34: He granted you everything you asked for. If you tried to count Allah's blessings, you could never number them. Humanity is truly unfair—deeply ungrateful.
ayahs.35: Recall when Abraham prayed: "My Rabb, make this city secure, and keep me and my children away from worship of idols.
ayahs.36: My Rabb, they have led many astray. Whoever follows me is with me; whoever disobeys me—You are still All-Forgiving, the Rahim whose special mercy awaits believers in the Akhirah.
ayahs.37: Our Rabb, I settled part of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House, so they may establish salah. Turn the hearts of believing people toward them and provide them fruits, so they may be grateful.
ayahs.38: Our Rabb, You know what we conceal and reveal. Nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Allah.
ayahs.39: All praise belongs to Allah who blessed me with Ishmael and Isaac in my old age. My Rabb is the Hearer of prayers.
ayahs.40: My Rabb, make me and those of my descendants who believe keep up salah. Our Rabb, accept my prayer.
ayahs.41: Our Rabb, forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day judgment arrives."
ayahs.42: Do not think Allah is unaware of what wrongdoers do. He only delays them until a Day when their eyes stare in horror—
ayahs.43: rushing forward, heads raised, never blinking, hearts empty.
ayahs.44: Warn people of the Day when punishment overtakes the wicked. Wrongdoers will cry: "Our Rabb, delay us a little—we will answer Your call and follow the messengers!" It will be said: "Did you not swear before that you would never be removed?"
ayahs.45: You passed the ruins of those who wronged themselves. It was made clear how We dealt with them, and We gave you many examples.
ayahs.46: They devised every plot known to Allah, but their plotting could not even overpower mountains—let alone Allah.
ayahs.47: Do not think Allah will fail His promise to His messengers. Allah is Almighty, capable of punishment.
ayahs.48: Watch for the Day when the earth will be changed into a different earth and the heavens as well, and all will appear before Allah—the One, the Supreme.
ayahs.49: On that Day you will see the wicked bound together in chains,
ayahs.50: in garments of tar, faces covered with flames.
ayahs.51: Allah will repay every soul for what it earned. Allah is swift in reckoning.
ayahs.52: This Quran is sufficient message for humanity—that they may take warning, know there is only One worthy of worship, and that people of reason may live with taqwa.
